meta.title: Operation of Hot Plate Dryer in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To provide controlled surface heating for evaporating small volumes of plant extracts on TLC plates, evaporating spot residues, and gentle warming of reagent solutions in Pharmacognosy practicals.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for TLC spot drying, gentle evaporation of solvent extract portions on watch glasses, and warming of reaction mixtures in phytochemical screening.
procedure: Place the hot plate dryer on a stable, heat-resistant bench surface.
Connect to the power supply and set the temperature control dial to the required setting.
Allow the hot plate surface to reach the set temperature — this typically takes 5–10 minutes.
Verify the surface temperature using an infrared thermometer or a calibrated bimetallic probe before placing samples.
For TLC plate drying: place the spotted TLC plate face-up on the hot plate surface at a low setting (40–50°C) for 1–2 minutes to drive off application solvent before development.
For extract evaporation: place the watch glass or evaporating dish with extract on the hot plate at 60–80°C; monitor continuously and stir with a glass rod.
Do not leave heating operations unattended — extract overheating causes decomposition and fire risk.
After the required drying or warming, remove samples using tongs or heat-resistant gloves.
Set the temperature control to zero and switch off after use.
Allow the hot plate surface to cool completely before cleaning.
Clean the plate surface with a damp cloth when cool — remove any dried residues carefully.
Record usage in the equipment logbook: date, operator, temperature used, and application.
precautions: Never place flammable organic solvents in open containers on a hot plate dryer — use a water bath inside a fume hood instead.
Always verify the surface temperature before placing heat-sensitive samples — thermostat readings may not accurately reflect actual surface temperature.
Use heat-resistant mats or ceramic tiles as intermediate surface for large or heavy objects.
Do not use on uneven or tilted surfaces — vessels can slide off.
The hot plate surface remains very hot after switch-off — place a 'HOT' warning sign on the unit until cool.
Never cover the hot plate surface — heat buildup can damage the heating element.
Do not use near flammable materials or near the edge of the bench.
